_comment: PRD §16.4 — model names are configuration, not code. Edit this file (or override via ADMIN, later) to change models without redeploying. Model slugs below are placeholders — verify current, correct IDs against https://openrouter.ai/models before going live.

profiles._comment: 2026-09-23: was meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct -- docs/COMMUNICATION_STYLE_EVAL.md Finding 5 caught it silently serving near-incoherent Kiswahili (called the user 'daktari wa Bitcoin' -- 'Bitcoin doctor') and a 3-line repetition loop under real load. runFallbackBakeoff.ts empirically tested 5 candidates (same prompts/pipeline, judged against the same communication rubric): gpt-4o-mini won clearly (1.75/2 avg score, 0/4 hard failures, 0 errors) vs. the old model's 1.00/2 with 2/4 hard failures and an outright error on one case. Full ranked results: chat_evaluations WHERE campaign_id='fallback_bakeoff_2026_09_23'. Still meaningfully cheaper than default_chat's Llama 3.3 70B, so the cost profile of 'fallback' vs 'primary' is preserved.

2026-09-17: default_chat (Llama 3.3 70B) was found via chat_evaluations to bookend Sheng/mixed_ke responses with corrected vocabulary (Niaje, Bro, we niambie tu) while leaving the explanatory body in formal Kiswahili sanifu -- a register ceiling a prompt fix alone didn't clear. Routes sheng/mixed_ke to a stronger model instead; see chatService.ts's selectModelProfile(). maxOutputTokens raised to 800 (vs default_chat's 500) after live eval showed Claude's answers truncating mid-word at 500 -- callers now request a generous 800 and each profile's own ceiling (not the caller) is what actually constrains Llama vs Claude.

Dataset Lab (docs/AFRIBIT_AI_SYNTHETIC_DATASET_ARCHITECTURE.md §3.2). Bulk generation — cheap, high volume. Verified against openrouter.ai/api/v1/models on 2026-09-14: $0.20/$1.20 per 1M tokens. Fallback added 2026-09-24 after Batch 004 hit the exact same class of gap dataset_critic/dataset_judge already had fixed the same session: openai/gpt-5.6-luna returned OpenRouter upstream rate-limit errors ("temporarily rate-limited upstream") on effectively every call with no fallback configured, failing the whole campaign run concept by concept. Added fallback_chat (gpt-4o-mini, already proven reliable) for the same reason it was added to the other two dataset-lab roles -- keeps the campaign moving through a transient provider-side rate limit instead of losing every concept to it.

Dataset Lab critic — used selectively on uncertain/sampled candidates, not every row (doc §10). Verified: $2/$12 per 1M. 2026-09-23: docs/COMMUNICATION_STYLE_EVAL.md's live eval hit this profile timing out 2-3x per 10-case run with no fallback configured -- runCommunicationEval.ts's judge call (this profile) is what scores every generated response, so a bare timeout meant losing that case's score entirely (crashing the whole run, before a separate try/catch fix). Added fallback_chat as a fallback -- same gpt-4o-mini already proven reliable+cheap in runFallbackBakeoff.ts's bake-off, and it supports the same OpenAI-style structured JSON output this profile's callers require. The fallback attempt runs at fallback_chat's own 400 tokens/temp 0.3 (Math.min-capped per gateway.ts's resolve()) rather than this profile's 800/0.2 -- fine for the small structured-JSON scoring payloads this profile is actually used for.

Dataset Lab judge — sparingly, only when generator/critic disagree or for difficult concepts (doc §3.2, §9). Verified: $2/$10 per 1M. Same fallback reasoning as dataset_critic above, added same day for consistency -- this profile shares the same characteristics (gpt-5.6 family, structured JSON output, no prior fallback) even though it wasn't the one observed timing out in this specific eval.

Community node (see docs/program/community-node.md). Model name is the Ollama tag; override per node with LOCAL_LLM_MODEL. Default is Gemma 3 12B: it passed all 15 cases of our Sheng/Kiswahili rubric in the October 2026 model search, while Qwen3 8B passed 3 (docs/evaluation/methodology.md). No fallback: if the node is down the API answers straight from the reviewed knowledge cards, so nothing leaves the community. timeoutMs is generous because a modest node must read a multi-thousand-token prompt before it emits its first word (measured: tens of seconds to minutes on 2014-era hardware).

INFERENCE_MODE=hybrid only: node first, then the hosted default_chat model if the node fails. This sends the user's question outside the community, so it is an explicit opt-in and must be disclosed to users.

The waiter's ticket call (apps/api/src/waiter/ticket.ts): rewrites the customer's Sheng/Kiswahili/English message into a clean English search question. Small, fast, cheap. ZDR routing is enforced by privacyProfile strict (OPENROUTER_ZDR_ONLY). google/gemma-3-12b-it has one zero-retention provider on OpenRouter (DeepInfra) as of 2026-10-02 -- a resilience point; failure falls back to the user's own words.
The waiter on a community node: the local model, no cloud call.

Optional cloud chat model: Gemma 3 12B passed 15/15 of our language rubric with the full prompt and 13/15 (11 accurate) with the compact prompt, versus Llama 3.3 70B's 11/15 with the full prompt. Select with CLOUD_CHAT_PROFILE=compact_chat_cloud after community review; falls back to default_chat.

The chef in the restaurant pipeline (apps/api/src/restaurant/chef.ts): a larger hosted model that sees only the waiter's scrubbed English ticket and the public knowledge cards, never the customer's own words. Zero-data-retention routing is enforced by privacyProfile strict. Llama 3.3 70B has many ZDR providers on OpenRouter (checked 2026-10-02).

The waiter's serving step on a node (restaurant pipeline, hybrid mode): the local model writes the answer in the customer's language from the chef's fact sheet. No fallback: if it fails, chat answers from the knowledge cards.

The waiter's serving step in cloud mode. NOTE: hosted, so it sees the customer's words -- in cloud mode the restaurant pipeline gives accuracy, not privacy. The privacy benefit needs a local waiter (hybrid mode).
